messages:
support-jen: heads up — acme-inc just escalated. Starting ~11:12 UTC they see ~20% 429s on generation API. Affected paths: /v1/generate and /v1/chat. Example request-id r12345ab. Response headers show X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, Retry-After: 30. They also reported increased p95 latency. This started after last night’s limiter config rollout. Can someone triage?

sre-oncall: on it — dropping into channel. Which cluster/region and which limiter config id? Any quick repro steps from customer?

support-jen: acme-prod in us-west2. They gave a short curl showing the 429: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate --data '{"prompt":"hello"}'` -> HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests + headers above. They said it happens during bursty traffic from their batch ingestion.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: service=limiter image=redwood/limiter:sha-8f3a1c4 rollout_id=limiter-v2-20260314 by alex at 2026-03-14T23:58:12Z

alex: I pushed the limiter config change last night — config name limiter-burst-policy-20260314. I added a more conservative refill to avoid token overshoot, but I might have messed a unit. Will inspect now.

miguel: grabbing limiter logs for acme tenant. Logs show repeated: `limiter: drop tenant=acme reason=token_exhausted route=/v1/generate tokens_left=0 burst_capacity=1000`. Also seeing `rate_limiter: refill_per_sec=2` in debug lines. That seems suspicious — we expect ~200 for that workload.

alex: ah — I accidentally set `refill_per_sec: 2` when I intended 200 (typo). The YAML unit was per-second but my local notes were per-minute. Sorry.

priya: if refill_per_sec is 2, small bursts will exhaust quickly and not recover during client bursts. For high-concurrency clients that will translate to sustained 429s. We should rollback or patch to the previous config asap.

sre-oncall: agreed — mitigation plan: 1) rollback limiter config to previous stable 20260313, 2) short-term tenant override for acme to increase their quota by 5x, 3) monitor p50/p95 errors and CPU. Who can run the rollback?

alex: I can rollback. Two options: revert config in configstore and trigger config reload, or do hot override for acme in the runtime. Which is faster?

miguel: hot override is faster for immediate customer impact — we can apply tenant override via the admin API: `POST /admin/tenants/acme/overrides {"refill_per_sec":500}`. But configstore rollback is cleaner and should follow.

sre-oncall: do both. Alex — apply hot override first. Priya — prepare configstore revert and rollout. I'll monitor.

alex: applying override now... `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://admin.redwood.ai/admin/tenants/acme/overrides -d '{"refill_per_sec":500,"duration_sec":900}'` -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK.

miguel: confirmed from limiter metrics: tokens_left for tenant=acme increased; 429 rate dropped to ~1% within 30s. Good.

priya: starting configstore rollback to limiter-burst-policy-20260313. Command: `rdctl config revert --key limiter-burst-policy --to-version 20260313 && rdctl reload limiter` (adjusted for our config tool). Planning canary rollout across 3 nodes before full rollout.

sre-oncall: posted canary plan. Also, add a short-term increase to the global burst cap so other tenants that briefly spike don't get impacted while rollback propagates. Alex — do you want me to escalate to infra for faster pod restart if needed?

alex: do it if rollout doesn't converge within 3 mins. For now I'm watching logs.

deploy-bot: configstore event: revert limiter-burst-policy -> from=20260314 to=20260313 triggered by priya at 2026-03-15T00:03:02Z

miguel: logs after override/rollback: `limiter: allow tenant=acme tokens_left=487 route=/v1/generate` — 429s practically gone. p95 latency trending back to baseline.

sre-oncall: rollback fully applied at 1938560300. Observability: 429 rate for acme from 20% -> 0.8% in 5 minutes; system-wide 429s spiked briefly but returned to normal.

support-jen: updated ACME support thread and told them we applied a temporary override and rolled back the config — they acknowledged and asked for postmortem.

priya: post-incident actions (short list):
- immediate: mark limiter-burst-policy-20260314 as faulty and disable auto-rollouts.
- short: add unit tests/CI guard that validates refill_per_sec values against expected ranges for existing tenants.
- medium: add canary delay policy for config updates affecting rate limiter (require 1h canary or traffic-based health checks).
- long: add a semantic validation step in configstore that rejects values that differ >10x from previous version unless explicitly acknowledged.

alex: owning rollback blamelessly. I'll open a PR with the unit test and request a review from priya and miguel. Also adding a lint rule to the config editor that warns on changes >x10.

sre-oncall: assign postmortem ticket: INC-193856-rlimit to alex (owner), priya (validation), miguel (metrics), due EOD tomorrow. Notify CS leads to prepare customer-facing summary.

miguel: quick note — we saw a secondary effect: some retries from clients caused short CPU spikes on limiter pods as threads retried, causing transient 5xxs. Mitigation: add short jittered backoff guidance in docs and consider server-side graceful 503 when CPU > 80% to avoid thundering herd.

support-jen: I'll coordinate customer comms. Please share a one-paragraph summary when postmortem is up.

sre-oncall: summary for channel: typo set refill_per_sec to 2 instead of 200 in limiter-burst-policy-20260314. Caused token exhaustion on bursty tenants and increased 429s. Mitigation: tenant override applied, configstore rollback to previous version, monitor confirmed recovery. Postmortem and CI guards planned.

alex: thanks all. marking incident resolved for now. I'll post the PR/issue links in here when ready. 

priya: closing loop — added CI lint PR: `github.com/redwood/config-lint/pull/457` (WIP).

sre-oncall: closing thread — if anyone sees residual customer reports reopen. Good catch support-jen :thumbsup:
